items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A data-driven accordion taking an array of items, with five distinct variants and an optional stack entrance that deals the items into place. Use it for FAQs and any list of collapsible sections.
items.docs: Named export: Accordion. Pass `accordionData` as { value, title, icon?, content } — content accepts a string array or a node. `type` is single | multiple; set `collapsible` to let the last open section close. Variants: default (open row lifts out as a card) | bordered (rail on the open row) | filled (open row inverts to primary) | elevated (cards, open one on a ring) | ghost (type and hairlines). `animation="stack"` piles the items and deals them out on scroll-in via the Web Animations API; skipped under reduced motion. Wraps the `ui-accordion` Radix primitive. For a single section, `collapsible` is lighter.

items.name: advanced-table
items.title: Advanced Table
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A stateful data table with search, typed sorting, pagination, row selection and batch actions — composed, so your data keeps its own shape.
items.docs: Named exports: DataTable plus DataTableHeading/Content/Header/Body/Row/Head/Cell/Footer/Empty, DataTableSearch, DataTablePageSize, DataTableSelect, DataTableSelectAll, DataTableBatchBar, DataTableInfo, DataTablePagination, DataTableExpandToggle, DataTableExpandedRow, DataTableTabs, DataTableFilter, DataTableReset, DataTableBatchAction, TableAction, TableRowAction, TableBadge, TablePerson, useDataTable, resolveAccessor. `DataTableTabs` and `DataTableFilter` filter one field each by exact match (`by` is a dot path or accessor); `useDataTable` exposes `filters`, `isFiltered` and `resetAll`. `variant="soft"` gives the admin-dashboard look. `DataTableBody` takes a render function receiving the current page of rows. `getRowId` defaults to id → _id → uuid; `sortBy` accepts a dot path or an accessor function (add `sortId` for functions). Builds on `table` and depends on `select` for the page-size control.

items.name: ai-chat
items.title: AI Chat
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An AI assistant interface with thread history sidebar, streaming-style responses and a prompt composer. Use it as the front end for an LLM feature.
items.docs: Named exports: AIChat, plus ChatThread, Message, ChatModel, EffortOption, ComposerTool, SendPayload and UploadHandler types. Responses are mocked — wire `onSend` ({ content, attachments, model, effort, tools }) to your endpoint and `uploadFile` (file, onProgress, signal) to your storage. The composer ships with a + menu (`tools`: one upload row opens the picker, the rest insert @Label mentions), drag-and-drop attachments (rocket progress indicator), a `models` picker, a Faster↔Smarter `efforts` slider that lights the prompt bar at the top level, and mic dictation via getUserMedia + the Web Speech API with graceful fallbacks. Variants: default | minimal | glass | compact (no history sidebar — opens as a hero with `heroTitle` over the prompt bar until the first message; `showSidebar={false}` does the same for any variant).

items.name: ai-chat-motion
items.title: AI Chat (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An AI assistant interface with thread history sidebar, streaming-style responses and a prompt composer. Use it as the front end for an LLM feature.
items.docs: Motion build of `ai-chat` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named exports: AIChat, plus ChatThread, Message, ChatModel, EffortOption, ComposerTool, SendPayload and UploadHandler types. Responses are mocked — wire `onSend` ({ content, attachments, model, effort, tools }) to your endpoint and `uploadFile` (file, onProgress, signal) to your storage. The composer ships with a + menu (`tools`: one upload row opens the picker, the rest insert @Label mentions), drag-and-drop attachments (rocket progress indicator), a `models` picker, a Faster↔Smarter `efforts` slider that lights the prompt bar at the top level, and mic dictation via getUserMedia + the Web Speech API with graceful fallbacks. Variants: default | minimal | glass | compact (no history sidebar — opens as a hero with `heroTitle` over the prompt bar until the first message; `showSidebar={false}` does the same for any variant).

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An inline alert with seven semantic types, five visual styles and optional dismiss. Use it for form-level and page-level messages that stay in the layout.
items.docs: Named export: Alert. `type` is primary | secondary | success | danger | warning | info | dark; `variant` is solid | outline | modern | glass | glow. Set `dismissible` with `onDismiss` to make it closable. For transient messages, use `toast` or `sonner`.

items.name: animated-faq
items.title: Animated Faq
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An FAQ section pairing an accordion of questions with a picture canvas that resizes and crossfades to each open answer. Use it for landing-page FAQs that should feel editorial rather than list-like.
items.docs: Named export: AnimatedFAQBlock (also the default export); the sample data `FAQ_ITEMS` lives in animated-faq-data.ts, which installs alongside. All motion is CSS — no animation library.

items.name: animated-faq-visuals
items.title: Animated Faq Visuals
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Theme-adaptive interactive visual preview components (CLI terminal, token customizer, MIT license certificate, performance HUD) for animated FAQ sections.
items.docs: Exports: CLIInstallationVisual, ThemingVisual, LicensingVisual, PerformanceVisual.

items.name: animated-list
items.title: Animated List
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A container component for rendering lists with animated item insertions, reorders, or removals. Ideal for dynamic notifications or feeds.
items.docs: Renders animated lists with smooth insertion and deletion transitions.

items.name: animated-timeline
items.title: Animated Timeline
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A timeline whose entries animate in on scroll, with five entrance styles. Use it on marketing pages for company history and roadmap sections.
items.docs: Named exports: AnimatedTimelineBlock, getThemeStyles (from animated-timeline-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `animation` is fade-up | slide-in | zoom-in | flip-up | blur-in; `layout` is left | right | center. Uses IntersectionObserver rather than a motion library, so it has no runtime dependencies. For status-driven progress, use `timeline`.

items.name: animated-typography
items.title: Animated Typography
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Headings and paragraphs that animate in with scramble, typewriter, rotating-word, blur and reveal effects. Use it for section titles that should draw the eye once.
items.docs: Named exports: AnimatedTypographyBlock, getThemeStyles (from animated-typography-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `as` picks the tag (h1-h6, p, span, blockquote) so semantics stay correct whatever the effect. The rotating variants (letter-bounce, typewriter, word-flip, blur-swap) cycle `words` between `titlePrefix` and `titleSuffix`, one every `interval` ms (or `index`, when something else keeps time); `text` stays what screen readers announce. `prefixPosition` is fixed (the text before the words holds still) or fluid (it re-centres as the word changes). `bare` hands the type to `className` for composing into a section heading, and `play={false}` holds a reveal until it is wanted. No runtime dependencies — CSS and timers only. For per-character motion, use `text-animation`.

items.name: api-playground
items.title: API Playground
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive API request builder with method selector, headers, query params and a response viewer. Use it in developer documentation so readers can try endpoints inline.
items.docs: Named exports: ApiPlaygroundBlock, getThemeStyles (from api-playground-theme.ts, which installs alongside), and the types ApiPlaygroundRequest, ApiMockHandler, ApiResponse. Methods GET | POST | PUT | PATCH | DELETE are colour-coded. Ships a mock response by default — pass a `mockHandler`, or wire it to a real fetch. Depends on `select`. Sending real requests from the browser is subject to CORS.

items.name: apple-select
items.title: Apple Select
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An iOS-style text selection rendered from a fixed character range — translucent highlight with lollipop handles on either end. Use it in docs, tutorials and marketing copy to point at part of a sentence.
items.docs:
Named export: AppleSelect. `text` is the full string and `selection` is a `[start, end]` character range (end exclusive, like String.slice) or an array of them for several phrases. The range is fixed by the author, not draggable. `color` takes any CSS colour, `handles={false}` drops the lollipops, and `animate` fades the highlight in on mount. Renders a

by default; `as="span"` sets it inline inside your own paragraph. Other HTML attributes are forwarded to it.

items.name: audio-player
items.title: Audio Player
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An audio player with artwork, transport, scrubber and volume, in a hero card, a compact bar, or wrapped around the browser's native controls.
items.docs: Named export: AudioPlayer. `audioUrl` and `artworkUrl` drive it; `variant` is hero | bar | native. Built on a plain <audio> element with no player library, so it adds no npm weight beyond the icons. Playback state mirrors the element's own events, which keeps it correct when a media key or the native controls change it. `skipSeconds` sizes the jump buttons (0 hides them) and the accent follows `--theme-color`.

items.name: avatar-stack
items.title: Avatar Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A row of overlapping faces that folds the rest into a +N disc and takes a trailing action. Use it as the social-proof cue under a headline or beside a count.
items.docs: Named export: AvatarStack. `avatars` are { src, alt? }; `size` sm | md | lg; `max` faces before the +N disc; `ringClassName` is the gap colour; `action` renders last at face size; `spreadOnHover` fans the faces apart under the pointer; `liftOnHover` raises the hovered face above its neighbours; `showTooltip` controls hover tooltips.

items.name: bento-showcase
items.title: Bento Showcase
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A six-card marketing bento on black: a hero with a live chat, a case-studies laptop, a headline, figures that scroll up, the plans on a phone, and a team strip that scrolls left. Use it as the showcase section of an agency or services landing page.
items.docs: Named export: BentoShowcase, with parts Card, Hero, CaseStudies, Headline, Stats, Phone and Team. Composed from the marquee, chat-bubble, half-stars, mobile-mockup and button items, which install alongside it. Headlines are children — wrap the display phrase in <em> for the serif italic; `Card` takes a `tone` and grid placement via className.

items.name: book-appointment
items.title: Book Appointment
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A practitioner's page that ends in an appointment: portrait and contact, scores as stars, two small charts, and a booking panel — glass or solid. Use it for clinics, salons, consultations.
items.docs: Named export: BookAppointment. Composed from the booking-card, glass-panel, half-stars and chart items, which install alongside it. Pass `practitioner`, `slotGroups` and `onBook`; `scores`, `visitReasons` and `activities` fill the stars, donut and bar; `variant` switches glass to solid.

items.name: book-flip
items.title: Book Flip
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive 3D Book Flip / Leaf Carousel component simulating realistic book page turns, open spreads, spine folds, and bottom leaf navigation controls.
items.docs: Supports leaves array prop, controlled currentIndex, keyboard navigation, and custom aspect ratios.

items.name: booking-card
items.title: Booking Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A booking panel for any card: a day strip paged a week at a time, time slots in groups, a button that reads back the choice, and a confirmation that draws itself in. Use it wherever a page ends in an appointment.
items.docs: Named export: BookingCard (plus the BookingSlot and Booking types). `BookingCard` is a compound component — put `BookingCard.Days`, `BookingCard.Slots`, `BookingCard.Submit` and `BookingCard.Confirmation` inside it in any layout; it holds the chosen day and slot and calls `onBook`. It draws no surface of its own: make it the padded inside of whatever panel it sits in so the confirmation reaches the edges. The selected day and slot, the submit and 'Add to calendar' buttons, the check mark and the focus rings use the `--primary` token.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A breadcrumb trail with per-item icons and automatic collapsing when the path is long. Use it to show position in a deep hierarchy.
items.docs: Named exports: BreadcrumbBlock, getThemeStyles (from breadcrumb-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `items` take { label, href?, icon? }; `maxItems` collapses the middle into an ellipsis past that count. Separator styles: classic | slash | solid | ghost. Renders next/link, so it needs edits outside Next.js.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A button with variants, sizes, loading state, and a click ripple effect. Reach for it as the default action element anywhere in an interface.
items.docs: Default export. Supports variant (default | destructive | outline | secondary | ghost | link), size (sm | lg), and a `loading` prop. Ripple keyframes are injected into document.head on mount, so no Tailwind config or global CSS changes are needed.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A full month calendar with event dots, range selection and a dashboard layout. Reach for it when dates need to be seen in context rather than just entered.
items.docs: Named exports: Calendar, CalendarDashboard, CalendarDayButton. Built on react-day-picker; variants are default | minimal | glass. `mockEvents` is a Record<string, string[]> keyed by date for the event dots. Pulls in `select` and `ui-button` as registry dependencies. For a plain date field, use `date-picker`.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A composable surface with header, title, description, content, and footer slots. Use it to group related content into a bounded block.
items.docs: Named exports: Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter. Compose them rather than passing props to a single element.

items.name: card-stack
items.title: Card Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A layered deck of cards featuring fluid drag-to-discard gestures, button-driven directional slide animations, and realistic depth perspective.
items.docs: Named export: CardStack (also default). Accepts items, visibleCards, swipeToDismiss, canDismissLastCard, loop, showHeader, and showNavigation.

items.name: card-stack-motion
items.title: Card Stack (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A layered deck of cards featuring fluid drag-to-discard gestures, button-driven directional slide animations, and realistic depth perspective.
items.docs: Motion build of `card-stack` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named export: CardStack (also default). Accepts items, visibleCards, swipeToDismiss, canDismissLastCard, loop, showHeader, and showNavigation.

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Three image carousels in one file — a plain slider, a full-bleed hero with autoplay, and a thumbnail-navigated gallery. Reach for it for product shots, galleries and landing-page heroes.
items.docs: Named exports: ImageCarousel, HeroCarousel, CustomCarousel. All three take an images array; HeroCarousel adds autoplay and CustomCarousel adds thumbnail navigation. Built on next/image, so remote hosts must be allowed in next.config.

items.name: carousel-3d
items.title: Carousel 3D
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A perspective carousel where cards rotate through depth, with drag and autoplay. Use it for portfolio and gallery sections that need presence.
items.docs: Named exports: ThreeDCarousel, CarouselItem. `items` take { id, title, category, image, description? }. `autoPlay` with `autoPlayInterval` advances it; dragging pauses. Renders a plain , so it works outside Next.js.

items.name: carousel-3d-motion
items.title: Carousel 3D (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A perspective carousel where cards rotate through depth, with drag and autoplay. Use it for portfolio and gallery sections that need presence.
items.docs: Motion build of `carousel-3d` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named exports: ThreeDCarousel, CarouselItem. `items` take { id, title, category, image, description? }. `autoPlay` with `autoPlayInterval` advances it; dragging pauses. Renders a plain , so it works outside Next.js.

items.name: cart
items.title: Cart
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A shopping cart with quantity controls, variant details and totals, rendered as drawer, modal, popover or full page. Use it for the cart step of a storefront.
items.docs: Named exports: CartBlock, getThemeStyles (from cart-theme.ts, which installs alongside), and the CartItem type. Switch presentation with `type` (drawer | modal | popover | page) without changing the item data. Pass the products in from the parent via `initialItems` — the component ships no sample data and renders its empty state without them. Items carry { id, name, price, quantity, gradient, size?, color? }; quantity and removal are handled internally. The trigger animates itself: a periodic tilt-and-ring nudge while the cart has items and has never been opened, a spring on press, and a badge pop whenever the count grows — all skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A dependency-free chart rendering bar, line, pie and donut from a single data array. Use it for simple dashboard visuals without pulling in a charting library.
items.docs: Named exports: ChartBlock. `data` takes { label, value, color? }; switch presentation with `type` (bar | line | pie | donut | donut-legend | stacked-bar) and set `height` in pixels for the axis charts. The two legend types colour each share from `colors` (theme accent first) and take `centerLabel` / `hoverLabel`. Hand-drawn SVG with no chart library, so bundle cost is nil — but there are no axes or scales beyond what is drawn. Use a real charting library for analytical work.

items.name: chat
items.title: Chat
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A complete messaging interface with contact list, conversation pane and composer. Use it as the shell for a support or direct-messaging feature.
items.docs: Named exports: ChatApp, plus Contact and CurrentUser types. A full application layout rather than a single element — it ships demo contacts and messages you replace with your own data. Variants: default | minimal | glass. For individual message bubbles, use `chat-bubble`.

items.name: chat-bubble
items.title: Chat Bubble
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Message bubble primitives with sent/received styling, grouping-aware corners, avatars and read receipts. Use them to build a custom message thread.
items.docs: Named exports: ChatBubble, ChatAvatar, ChatMessage, ChatTimestamp. `layout` is default | group-top | group-middle | group-bottom and adjusts the corner radii so consecutive messages from one sender read as a block. `status` renders sent | delivered | read ticks. These are the pieces `chat` assembles.

items.name: circular-text
items.title: Circular Text
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Words set on a circle, turning slowly, with room in the middle for a mark, a play button or a link. Use it for video badges, stamps and 'see the work' links.
items.docs: Named export: CircularText. `text` repeats to fill the ring (or `repeat` times), `size` in px, `speed` seconds per turn (0 holds still), `direction`, `fontSize`/`tracking` in units of a 100-wide circle, `color` (currentColor follows the parent), `innerRing`. Children sit in the middle. Holds still under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: collage-hero
items.title: Collage Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A playful hero: a badge whose name turns around a mark, a serif headline with two coloured words, hashtag pills, a five-column photo collage and a footer with a quote, a scroll pill and a watch-video trigger. Use it for a kindergarten, studio, school or any warm, busy place.
items.docs: Named export: CollageHero (plus CollageHero.Badge and CollageHero.Photo). Composed from the button, circular-text and dialog items, which install alongside it. Pass `brand`, `heading` (with <em> for the coloured words), `tags`, `caption`, seven `photos`, `quote`, `scrollLabel`/`scrollTo` and `video` ({ text, url }). `accent` sets --primary for the section, `highlight` the second colour; `reveal` is in-view or immediate.

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A minimal show/hide disclosure with controlled and uncontrolled modes. Use it for a single expandable region where a full accordion is overkill.
items.docs: Named exports: Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent. Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled, or `open` with `onOpenChange` to drive it yourself. For several linked sections, use `accordion`.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive 360° Color Spectrum Wheel and Color Palette component featuring 2D color picking, lightness & alpha sliders, format toggles (HEX, RGB, HSL), one-click copy, and EyeDropper API support.
items.docs: Named export: ColorPicker. Pass `value` and `onChange`. Set `variant` to 'standalone' for full card or 'popover' for trigger dropdown. Supports `showPresets`, `showAlpha`, and `showEyeDropper`.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A command palette with fuzzy search, grouped results and a dialog mode. Use it for the ⌘K quick-action menu in an application.
items.docs: Named exports: Command, CommandDialog, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandSeparator. Use CommandDialog with `open` / `onOpenChange` for the overlay form, or Command inline. Set `shouldFilter` false to filter server-side yourself. Bind your own ⌘K listener — no global shortcut is registered for you.

items.name: component-wall
items.title: Component Wall
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A landing hero for a component library: a headline that blurs in word by word and keeps one word turning, a lead, an install command that names whichever card a camera has just landed on, two actions, a line of trust and the tools it is built with in batches — centred between two walls of screenshots that never end, one camera resting high and the other low, or on the left of a single wall.
items.docs:
Named export: ComponentWall (plus the ComponentWallItem type). Composed from the image-wall, text-animation, copy-button, avatar-stack and half-stars items, which install alongside it, and takes a tech-stack in its `stack` slot. Pass `badge` ({ label, href? }), `heading` (a string, revealed word by word; write `{word}` where `headingWords` take turns every `wordInterval` ms, and name one word in `accent` for the primary colour), `description` (a string or inline JSX — it renders inside a

), `install` ({ command } — write `{item}` where the focused card's `slug` goes, e.g. `npx shadcn@latest add @avara-ui/{item}`), `primaryAction`/`secondaryAction` ({ label, href, icon? }), `trust` ({ text, avatars?, rating? }), `items` ({ title, image, slug? }[] — every screenshot sits in the same 493:332 frame; slug defaults to the title in kebab-case) and `stack` (a node — a of s of : the tools over the lower wall on desktop and under the band on phones; in the centred layout it closes the copy column, where the compact variant fits). `columns`, `interval` (ms the camera rests; 0 holds still), `order` (serial | shuffle), `zoom`, `intro` (ms the camera drifts with nothing in focus while the copy arrives; default 1800) and `onFocus` pass straight to the wall; `layout` is split (copy left, wall right), center (copy between two walls — the left camera resting high, the right low, taking turns, the second wall dealing the same items from halfway through; the tools sit under the copy; zoom defaults to 0.9; below lg a single band of every card sits between the copy and the tools), or center-background (`persistentBackground`); `showMobileWall` (boolean, default true: set to false to completely hide wall animations on small screens

items.name: compute
items.title: Compute
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A compute-resource panel showing instance sizing and usage as a settings-style card. Use it as a starting point for an infrastructure or plan-usage screen.
items.docs: Named export: ComputeBlock. A self-contained example with hardcoded values and local state — copy and adapt rather than configuring through props. Depends on `ui-base` for ComponentCard.

items.name: confidential-folder
items.title: Confidential Folder
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive confidential folder sleeve with a card that slides out horizontally on hover and gracefully elevates on click.
items.docs: Named export: ConfidentialFolder, OrbitalSpirograph.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A right-click context menu that opens at the pointer, with items, separators and shortcut hints. Use it for secondary actions on a row or canvas object.
items.docs: Named exports: ContextMenu, ContextMenuTrigger, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut. The trigger suppresses the native browser menu inside its bounds. Positioned from pointer coordinates, so it opens where the user clicked rather than anchored to an element.

items.name: conversation-timeline
items.title: Conversation Timeline
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A dense rail of thin marks, one per message, that expands into a labelled list on hover — a minimap for long chats. Use it beside a conversation to jump between messages.
items.docs: Named export: ConversationTimeline (plus the TimelineCheckpoint type). `checkpoints` is `{ id, label, sublabel?, role? }[]`, `activeId` marks the selected row with `accent` and `onSelect` receives a clicked id. `side` puts labels left or right; `rowHeight` / `collapsedRowHeight` set the expanded and resting row sizes, `visibleCount` caps rows before scrolling and `labelWidth` fixes the label column. Hover or focus expands it; touch devices stay expanded; respects prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A clipboard button that confirms the copy in place — the icon pops to a check and the label swaps to "Copied!" — plus a read-only Copy Field for links, tokens and commands. Use it anywhere a value needs to be copied without a toast.
items.docs: Named exports: CopyButton, CopyField; the useCopyToClipboard hook is exported from copy-button-hooks.ts, which installs alongside. `value` is the text copied; `label` / `copiedLabel` / `errorLabel` set the three states, `timeout` how long the confirmation lingers, `iconOnly` drops the label. Variants are solid | soft | outline | ghost, sizes sm | md | lg, `color` a preset or hex. CopyField wraps a read-only input with the button beside it (or `inset` inside it) and forwards `buttonProps`. Falls back to execCommand where the Clipboard API is unavailable.

items.name: counter
items.title: Counter
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A number component in four modes — stepper, count-up, circular progress and countdown. Use it for quantity inputs and animated statistics.
items.docs: Named exports: CounterBlock, getThemeStyles (from counter-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `type` is stepper | animated | circular | countdown — stepper is an input with min/max, the others are display-only. Variants: default | outline | soft | vertical for the stepper; `slide` for the countdown (soft tiles, only the figure that changed slides — the same countdown the waitlist item uses). The countdown takes `targetDate` (Date, ISO string or timestamp) and `doneLabel`. The animated type also takes `bare` (just the figure, no card), `decimals`, `startOnView` (count once visible) and `className`. `color` accepts a theme name, a hex code or `inherit`.

items.name: counter-section
items.title: Counter Section
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A collection of 4 animated high-impact Counter and Stats Sections with viewport-triggered count-up easing, zero shadows, and full adaptive styling.
items.docs: Named export: CounterSection. Accepts variant ('cyber-hud' | 'minimal-slash' | 'halftone-cinema' | 'spotlight-gradient') and custom stats array with value, prefix, suffix, decimals, label, sublabel, and tag.

items.name: cta-section
items.title: Cta Section
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interconnected Brand Pillars call-to-action component featuring interactive service cards, a synchronized scorecard with animated progress meters, and a highlight popover bar.
items.docs: Named exports: CTASection, CtaSection, and the PillarItem type. Accepts variant ('brand-pillars' | 'minimal' | 'split'), pillars array, custom heading, statement, summary metrics, and active accent color.

items.name: cursor-animation
items.title: Cursor Animation
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A custom cursor with magnetic, glow, trail, spotlight and crosshair effects, scoped to its children. Use it on portfolio and agency sites.
items.docs: Named export: CursorAnimation. `variant` is magnetic | glow | trail | badge | spotlight | expand | crosshair; `trailCount` sets trail length and `label` fills the badge variant. Wrap a region rather than the page so normal cursors survive elsewhere. Pointer-only — no effect on touch.

items.name: curved-carousel
items.title: Curved Carousel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A continuously scrolling carousel whose cards follow a curved arc path. Use it for logo walls and showcase strips that should feel ambient.
items.docs: Named exports: CurvedCarousel, CurvedCarouselCard. `speed` sets the drift rate and `autoPlay` toggles motion. Loops continuously rather than paging, so it suits decorative rows more than navigable content.

items.name: custom-code-block
items.title: Custom Code Block
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A tabbed code viewer with filenames, language badges and per-tab copy. Use it in documentation to show the same example across several files.
items.docs: Named exports: CustomCodeBlock, CodeTab. `tabs` take { code, language, fileName }; a single tab renders without the tab strip. Uses `lucide-react` for file-type icons. Highlighting is a built-in regex tokenizer, not Shiki or Prism — good for snippets, not a full editor.

items.name: dashboard
items.title: Dashboard
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An admin dashboard home: greeting with all-time totals, a period switch, an overview chart with a tab per metric, activity feed, traffic sources, visitors by country and top authors. Three looks: classic, glass, and liquid-glass (using LiquidGlassWrapper, LiquidGlassBackground, and LiquidGlassSvgFilter).
items.docs: Named exports: Dashboard (also the default) plus LiquidGlassWrapper, LiquidGlassBackground, LiquidGlassSvgFilter, and the DashboardMetric, DashboardPoint, DashboardTotal, DashboardActivity, DashboardShare, DashboardAuthor, DashboardPayment, DashboardShortcut, DashboardLinks, DashboardPeriod and DashboardVariant types. variant: 'classic' (default) | 'glass' | 'liquid-glass'; all read the same props, and glass/liquid-glass also read `payments`, `shortcuts`, `totals[].metric` / `href` and `activity[].person` / `avatar`. Every number comes from props: `metrics` carry a series per period (day | week | month, oldest first) and an optional `change` per period; `sources`, `countries` and `authors` are keyed by period; `activity` items have a type of user | post | payment | message. Pass `linkComponent` (e.g. next/link) for the panel links and `onExport` to replace the built-in CSV. Composes toggle-group (segmented), chart and popover. Clock-dependent text renders after mount, so server and client markup agree.

items.name: data-flow
items.title: Data Flow
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sources → core → outputs section: platform cards on the left feed one node in the middle, which fans out to result cards on the right, with curved connectors that draw in on first view and then carry a moving dash. Use it to explain a pipeline, an integration, or where an AI product's data comes from.
items.docs: Named export: DataFlow, with parts Source, Core, Output, Pill, Tag and Row. Composed from the flowchart and apple-select items, which install alongside it (`intro` + `highlights` render through AppleSelect); the docs example also uses half-stars and button inside its output cards. Connectors are measured from the cards at runtime (ResizeObserver), hidden below lg; `reveal` is in-view or immediate; `accent` pins the dash colour, otherwise it follows --primary. Wrap intro phrases in <mark> for black pills.

items.name: data-grid
items.title: Data Grid
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An editable spreadsheet-style grid with inline cell editing and keyboard navigation. Use it when users need to change values in place rather than just read them.
items.docs: Named exports: DataGridBlock, getThemeStyles (from data-grid-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `columns` take { field, headerName, width?, type?, readOnly? } — `type` number constrains input. Editing is local to the component, so persist changes through your own handler. Zero runtime dependencies.

items.name: data-maps
items.title: Data Maps
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A choropleth world map colouring countries by metric, with fill and dot variants. Use it for geographic analytics and regional breakdowns.
items.docs: Named exports: DataMaps, DataPoint. `dataPoints` take { id, name, active, new, color?, flag? } keyed by country id; `variant` is fill | dots, with `center` and `zoom` for the initial view. **Import Leaflet's CSS yourself** and supply your own GeoJSON. Uses next/image, so it needs edits outside Next.js.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date Picker
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A single-date field with a popover calendar, typed entry and validation states. Use it for one-off dates such as a deadline or birth date.
items.docs: Named exports: DatePickerBlock, getThemeStyles (from date-picker-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Controlled via `value: Date | null` and `onChange`. Shares the variant, color and size vocabulary of the `input` item, so the two line up visually in the same form. For month grids or event display, use `calendar` instead.

items.name: design-components-folder
items.title: Design Components Folder
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An animated folder that opens to fan out component preview cards. Use it on portfolio and feature pages to reveal a collection on interaction.
items.docs: Named export: DesignComponentsFolder. Motion drives the open and card-fan animation; `color` tints the folder. Uses next/image, so it needs edits outside Next.js. For the empty folder shape, use `design-folder-box`.

items.name: design-folder-box
items.title: Design Folder Box
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A frosted-glass folder shape with title and subtitle, used as a decorative container. Use it on portfolio and feature sections where a plain card is too plain.
items.docs: Named export: DesignFolderBox. Presentational only — `color` tints the glass. For the version that holds stacked cards inside the folder, use `design-components-folder`.

items.name: designs-toolkit
items.title: Designs Toolkit
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A pinned resource toolkit grid featuring authentic 3D pushpins, staggered cards, brand icon badges, and connected corkboard path lines.
items.docs: Named exports: DesignsToolkitBlock (default), ToolkitItem.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A composable modal dialog with focus trapping, overlay and controlled or uncontrolled open state. Use it as the general-purpose dialog primitive.
items.docs: Named exports: Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogFooter, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, useDialog (from dialog-context.ts, which installs alongside), plus the DialogSize type. Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled, or `open` with `onOpenChange` to drive it — `onOpenChange` also fires on Escape and backdrop clicks, which is where you refuse a dismissal while async work is in flight. Size the panel with `size`: sm | md | lg | xl | full, where full fills the viewport and drops the rounding, border and height cap; `className` is merged after it and wins. `hideCloseButton` drops the built-in X. Dialogs nest — render one inside another's content and the inner one portals above its parent, with Escape and backdrop clicks reaching only the topmost. For a controlled overlay you drive entirely from your own state, use `modal`.

items.name: dock
items.title: Dock
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A macOS-style dock where icons magnify as the pointer approaches. Use it for app launchers and playful navigation bars.
items.docs: Named exports: Dock, DockItem. `items` take { id, label, icon, onClick?, isActive?, badge? }. `magnification` sets peak scale and `distance` the falloff radius. Pointer-driven — on touch devices it degrades to a plain icon row.

items.description: An interactive reorderable card list with 60fps Motion spring physics, right-side grip handles, and custom card metadata.
items.docs: Named exports: DraggableCardList, DraggableCardItem. Accepts `items` ({ id, title, description, date, badge, linkText, linkUrl, completed }), `onReorder`, `title`, `dragHandlePosition` ('right' | 'left'), `enableCheckboxes`, and `enableBadges`.

Accepts `items` ({ id, title, description, date, badge, linkText, linkUrl, completed }), `onReorder`, `title`, `dragHandlePosition` ('right' | 'left'), `enableCheckboxes`, and `enableBadges`.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A panel that slides in from any screen edge, with overlay and GSAP easing. Use it for mobile navigation, filters and detail panels.
items.docs: Named exports: Drawer, DrawerOverlay, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription, DrawerFooter. `side` chooses the entry edge. Controlled via `open` and `onOpenChange`. Note it also exports a local `Button` used by its demo — import your own for real use.

items.name: email
items.title: Email
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A full email client layout with folders, labels, message list, reading pane and attachments. Use it as the shell for an inbox or ticketing view.
items.docs: Named exports: EmailApp, plus Email, EmailLabel and Attachment types. The largest block in the registry — a complete application layout with demo data to replace, not a single element. Variants: default | minimal | glass.

items.name: error
items.title: Error
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A responsive, animated Cyberpunk Diagnostic Terminal Error Website Section with full Light and Dark mode adaptive styling, diagnostic monitors, and live stacktrace inspection.
items.docs: Named export: ErrorSection (also default export) and ErrorSectionProps. Designed to serve as a full-page 500, 404, or runtime error boundary with light & dark theme support, one-click incident copying, and reboot action triggers.

items.name: falling-tags
items.title: Falling Tags
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A physics-based interactive tags playground where badges float, fall under gravity, collide realistically, and can be dragged and thrown.
items.docs: Named exports: FallingTagsBlock (default), FallingTagItem, FallingTagPalette.

items.name: fan-stack
items.title: Fan Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Overlapping cards in a tilted diagonal cascade, dealt out of one pile into place as the stack scrolls into view. Use it for a short numbered sequence — steps, phases, a three-part system.
items.docs: Named exports: FanStack, FanStackCard, FanStackTitle, FanStackStep, FanStackDescription, FanStackPoints, FanStackPoint, FanStackThumb (plus the FanStackTone and FanStackThumbSide types). Compose cards as children — any number works; each card's `tone` (muted | light | accent) and its thumb's `side` (right | left | top) default by position. `FanStackThumb` takes your own `` or framework image as its child. Colours derive from `--primary`. The cascade is a container query: below 768px of width the cards become a CSS sticky stack, each sliding over the last (`stickyTop` clears a fixed header). The deal is scrubbed by scroll (`scrub` seconds of lag, 0 to lock it); pass `scrollerRef` when it scrolls inside a container. The deal is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: faq-section

items.docs: Named export: FAQSection (also default export); AnimatedFAQBlock and the FAQItem type are also exported; the sample data FAQ_ITEMS lives in faq-section-data.ts, which installs alongside.

items.name: fashion-hero
items.title: Fashion Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A fashion hero: a bold headline between a turning video badge and a stack of faces, five staggered columns of looks on flat colour that tilt under the pointer, a call to action on the middle look, and a footer with a quote and the next story. Use it for a clothing store, a lookbook or an editorial landing page.
items.docs: Named export: FashionHero (plus FashionHero.Look). Composed from the circular-text, avatar-stack, text-animation, tilted-card and dialog items, which install alongside it. Pass `heading`, up to seven `looks` ({ src, alt, tone, blend?, position? }), `video` ({ badge, url }), `avatars` + `avatarsHref`, `cta`, `quote`, `teaser` and `linkComponent`; `accent` sets --primary, `reveal` is in-view or immediate.

items.name: flavour-carousel
items.title: Flavour Carousel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A product hero for anything that comes in flavours: the product stands in a mountain of powder against a moss backdrop and its flavours flank it on four tilted cream tiles. It rises from behind the powder spinning and settles; then every five seconds, or on a click, the chosen tile slides into the cup and the cup cross-fades to that flavour without moving; a glow takes the flavour's colour, a price pill and add-to-cart hang under the cup. One component for both themes: in dark mode the tiles go translucent black.
items.docs: Named export: FlavourCarousel. Composed from the button item, which installs alongside it. Pass `flavours` ({ name, price?, tint?, product, tile }[] — every product image must share the same crop), `heading`, `interval` in ms (0 turns autoplay off), `initial`, `reveal` (in-view, immediate or none), `onChange` and `onAdd` (omit it to hide the cart button) with `addLabel`. `backgroundImage` is the backdrop and `foregroundImage` the transparent powder cutout laid in front of the cup (`foregroundHeight` of the stage tall); without them the scene is drawn from `background`, `mound` ([light, dark]) and `paper`.

items.name: fleet-map
items.title: Fleet Map
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A live fleet tracking view pairing a Leaflet map with a vehicle list and status filters. Use it for logistics and delivery dashboards.
items.docs: Named exports: FleetTracker, Vehicle. `fleetData` take { id, location, lat, lng, status, speed? } with status active | idle | maintenance. **Import Leaflet's CSS yourself** — `import "leaflet/dist/leaflet.css"` — or the map renders as broken tiles. Leaflet touches `window`, so load it client-side only.

items.name: floating-contact-button
items.title: Floating Contact Button
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A floating support bubble that expands into a chat panel, with state persisted to localStorage. Use it for live chat and contact widgets on marketing sites.
items.docs: Named export: FloatingContactButtonBlock. `position` is bottom-right | bottom-left; `containerMode` fixed pins it to the viewport while absolute scopes it to a parent. Open state survives reloads via `localStorageKey`. Messages are local — connect your own backend.

items.name: flow-gallery
items.title: Flow Gallery
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Horizontal and diagonal 3D cascading gallery stream with continuous downward auto-flow motion, drag inertia physics, and isometric perspective depth.
items.docs: Named export: FlowGallery. Interactive drag with grab cursor, continuous downward auto-flow, 3D isometric plane, and Next Themes adaptation.

items.name: flowchart
items.title: Flowchart
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A node-and-connector flow diagram with highlightable paths and GSAP transitions. Use it to explain a pipeline or decision flow.
items.docs: Named exports: Flowchart, FlowCanvas, FlowNode, FlowConnection, useFlowchart. Nodes declare `connectedPaths`; setting the active path highlights every node and connection on it. Positions are authored by you — there is no auto-layout. `layout="fluid"` drops the fixed canvas so connections can be drawn over your own layout; `FlowConnection` takes `dashed`, `flowDash`, `glow` and `drawDuration`.

items.name: folder
items.title: Folder
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A tactile folder — skeleton cards or your own photos tuck behind a frosted-glass pocket and fan out into an arc on hover. Use it for file groups, galleries and drag-and-drop upload targets.
items.docs: Named exports: Folder, SkeletonCard (plus FolderFile / FolderProps types). `files` is { thumb?, name?, progress? }[]; without files, `peek` skeleton cards show. `color` tints body, pocket, icon and cards via OKLCH; `icon` is a lucide component. Hover, tap or focus opens the fan; past five files it pages with arrows or by dragging a card. `interactive` adds drag-and-drop + click-to-browse with `onFiles`, `progress` and `onRemoveFile`. Pulls in `tooltip` for file-name hovers.

All variants adapt across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Form scaffolding — wrapper, field, error and submit — with a shared color theme and a glitch error variant. Use it to keep field spacing and validation styling consistent across a form.
items.docs: Named exports: FormWrapper, FormField, FormError, FormSubmit, getThemeStyles (from form-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Layout and styling only — bring your own state, via react-hook-form or otherwise. FormSubmit takes `isSubmitting` to render its pending state.

items.name: gallery
items.title: Gallery
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A versatile, multi-variant interactive visual gallery featuring revolving 3D orbit rings, responsive bento grids, vertical continuous reels, 3D pill carousels, and perspective arc carousels. Use it for agencies, portfolios, product showcases, and creative hero sections.
items.docs: Named export: Gallery (also exports OrbitGallery for backward compatibility). Default export: Gallery. Variants: orbit | bento | reel | pill | arc. Pass items ({ image, alt, title?, subtitle?, href? }), speed/duration, orientation, aspect, autoSlide, and radius/gap options.

items.name: glass-panel
items.title: Glass Panel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A frosted surface in four shapes and the aurora ground it sits on. Use it for glass bento layouts, profile and booking pages — or flip it to solid cards with one prop.
items.docs: Named exports: GlassBackdrop, GlassPanel (plus SurfaceVariant, GlassShape types); useSurface is exported from glass-panel-context.ts, which installs alongside. `GlassBackdrop` washes three `aurora` colours behind a 12-column grid (`gridClassName` for row heights and gaps) and sets `variant` (glass | solid) for every `GlassPanel` inside; panels take `shape` (slab, tile, disc, capsule), `interactive`, and Tailwind column spans.

items.name: globe
items.title: Globe
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive 3D WebGL globe visualization with location markers, arc curves, and rotation controls. Use it for global presence and location showcases.

items.name: half-stars
items.title: Half Stars
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A star rating supporting half-star precision, in read-only or interactive mode. Use it for reviews and any score shown out of five.
items.docs: Named export: HalfStars. Set `interactive` to let users pick a rating and `allowHalf` for half-star steps. `onHoverChange` fires during hover so you can preview the value before commit. Leave `interactive` off to render a static score.

items.name: heart-signal
items.title: Heart Signal
items.author: AlgorizeTech

items.docs: Named export: HeartSignal. Supports 2 smooth variants (ecg-line and cardiac-wave), live BPM telemetry badge, speed control, and active theme color integration.

items.name: hero
items.title: Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A prop-driven hero section supporting revolving 3D orbit ring, spring word bounce, character typewriter, 3D split marquee slider, pet-shop, doctor, and facility CAD grid variants.
items.docs: Named export: HeroBlock. Everything is a prop — `variant` switches between 'orbit', 'bounce', 'typing', 'slider', 'pet-shop', 'doctor', and 'facility', with interactive animations, theme color support, and responsive layouts.

items.name: hero-carousel
items.title: Hero Carousel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A full-bleed photo hero with a queue of cards: the front card is the slide on screen, the ones behind it are what comes next. Every five seconds or on a click the queue slides forward, the photograph behind crossfades and the headline and caption follow. A glass panel carries the faces of past guests, an intro and the call to action.
items.docs: Named export: HeroCarousel. Composed from the avatar-stack item, which installs alongside it. Pass `slides` ({ image, alt, title, description?, heading?, position? }), `eyebrow`, `heading`, `intro`, `avatars` + `avatarsLabel`, `cta` ({ label, href }) and `linkComponent`. `interval` is the autoplay gap in ms (0 turns it off), `accent` sets --primary, `reveal` is in-view or immediate, `onChange` reports the front slide.

items.name: homepage-hero
items.title: Homepage Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A feature-rich hero section with animated typing text, interactive CLI copy badge, gradient action buttons, and feature list.

items.name: honeycomb-hero
items.title: Honeycomb Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A travel hero on a dark ground that shifts colour: a light line over a huge white word whose letters turn the theme's primary where they cross the photographs, and a honeycomb of hexagonal photographs with a primary hexagonal call to action set among them. The large hexagon is the slide on screen; its photograph fills the background, tinted with that photograph's own tone, so the whole section changes colour as, every four seconds or on the arrows at the foot, every hexagon moves one step along the ring, endlessly.
items.docs: Named export: HoneycombHero. Pass `title` and `titleAccent` (its letters that cross the photographs take `titleOverlapColor`, the primary by default), `subtitle`, `primaryActionLabel` (a \n breaks the line; a compass sits above it in the hexagon) and `primaryActionHref`, `images` ({ src, alt, tone? }[] in queue order — nine cells are visible; tone is the deep colour behind everything while that photograph is featured), `socialLinks`, `interval` in ms (0 turns autoplay off) and `onChange`. The overlapping letters, rule, arrows and call to action follow the theme's primary (the hexagon's compass and label primary-foreground); `accent` sets --primary for the section, `background` is the tone for photographs without one (a deep shade of the primary by default); `linkComponent` takes next/link.

items.name: horizontal-rail
items.title: Horizontal Rail
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A horizontal sliding rail layout with smooth drag inertia, snapping cards, and navigation controls. Use it for showcasing products, media cards, or horizontal content.

items.name: horizontal-scroll-stack
items.title: Horizontal Scroll Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A section that converts vertical scrolling into horizontal card movement with a progress indicator. Use it for process timelines and step sequences.
items.docs: Named export: HorizontalScrollStack. Items take { id, number, title, description, icon? }. Pins the section and maps scroll progress to horizontal travel, so it needs enough page height to complete — and it takes over scrolling while pinned, which is worth testing on touch.

items.name: icons
items.title: Icons
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A set of 26 brand SVG icons — Google, GitHub, Apple, Microsoft, Slack, LinkedIn and more — as React components. Use them for social sign-in buttons and provider lists.
