items.name: image-compare
items.title: Image Compare
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A before/after image slider with five handle styles and drag or click positioning. Use it for retouching, redesign and product comparison sections.
items.docs: Named export: ImageCompare. `beforeImage` and `afterImage` take URLs, with `beforeLabel` / `afterLabel` for the badges and `initialPosition` as a 0-100 percentage. Variants: classic-slider | split-handle | glowing-divider | badge-overlay | minimal. Both images should share an aspect ratio or the reveal will misalign.

items.name: image-viewer
items.title: Image Viewer
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A collection of 4 responsive E-commerce Image Viewer components featuring inner lens magnifying zoom, HD side portal projection, carousel sliders, and interactive thumbnail strips.
items.docs: Named export: ImageViewer. Accepts `variant` (4 variants: inner-zoom, side-zoom, slider, thumbnails), `thumbnailPosition` (left, right, bottom), `images`, `colors`, `badge`, `showWishlist`, `enableLightbox`, `className`. Includes built-in fullscreen lightbox modal with keyboard and arrow controls.

items.name: image-wall
items.title: Image Wall
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A wall of screenshots that never ends, and a camera hanging over it: it rests zoomed in on one card, then every few seconds pulls back, glides to the next and settles on it. Use it wherever a set of images should keep showing itself — a hero, a gallery band, a showcase.
items.docs: Named export: ImageWall (plus the WallItem type). Pass `items` ({ title, image }[] — every image is cropped from its top edge into the same 493:332 frame) and give it a height with `className`; it fills its box. `columns` sets the tile, `interval` the rest between flights in ms (0 holds still), `order` is serial (card by card) or shuffle (every card once per round, at random), `zoom` the resting scale — a box under 420px tall eases it down to 0.72 so a few cards fit, one under 640px wide to 0.5 so the flight between cards stays visible on a phone; `intro` (ms) drifts the camera, pulled back with nothing in focus, before its first landing; `anchor` ({ x?, y? }, shares of the box, default the middle) is where the resting card sits; `onFocus` reports the card in view. The camera holds while hovered, while the tab is hidden and while off screen; under prefers-reduced-motion it cuts instead of flying.

items.name: infrastructure-topology
items.title: Infrastructure Topology
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive live data flow infrastructure topology graph with animated SVG beams, central neural mesh hub, service cards, and metrics.
items.docs: Named export: InfrastructureTopology. Accepts `headerTitle`, `headerSubtitle`, `statusBadge`, `bandwidthBadge`, `centerTitle`, `nodes`, `metrics`, `animated`, `interactive`.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A text input with label, helper text, error state, icon slots and password reveal. Reach for it as the default field in any form.
items.docs: Named exports: InputBlock, getThemeStyles (from input-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Accepts type (text | password | email | number | file), variant (default | filled | underlined | glow), inputSize, and a color token (indigo | rose | emerald | zinc, or your own). Pass `error` to switch it into the invalid state; `helperText` renders below when there is no error.

items.name: invoice
items.title: Invoice
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A printable invoice with line items, tax and totals, in three presentation styles. Use it for billing summaries and receipt pages.
items.docs: Named exports: Invoice, getThemeStyles (from invoice-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `InvoiceData` carries invoiceNumber, parties, dates and an `items` array of { item, description?, hours|qty, rate }. Totals are computed for you. Variants: default | minimal | glass.

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A row primitive pairing media, title, description and actions in one aligned layout. Use it to build list rows, notification entries and search results.
items.docs: Named export: ItemBlock. `media` and `actions` take arbitrary nodes, so an avatar and a button drop straight in. Variants: default | compact | card | bordered. Passing `onClick` makes the whole row interactive.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An inline keyboard-key badge for rendering shortcuts. Use it in menus, tooltips, and docs where a keystroke needs to look pressable.
items.docs: Compose several side by side for chords, e.g. <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> <Kbd>K</Kbd>.

items.name: loader
items.title: Loader
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A loading indicator in five shapes — spinner, dots, pulse, ring and bar — with an optional caption. Use it for inline and full-panel pending states.
items.docs: Named exports: LoaderBlock, getThemeColor. `variant` picks the shape, `size` is sm | md | lg | xl, and `text` renders a caption beneath. Pure CSS animation with no runtime dependencies. For content-shaped placeholders, use `skeleton`.

items.name: login-form
items.title: Login Form
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sign-in form with social buttons, password reveal, remember-me and multiple layout variants including ribbon-drift and liquid-glass. Use it as the entry point of an authenticated app.
items.docs: Default export: LoginForm. Also exports LoginBlock, getThemeStyles (from login-form-theme.ts, which installs alongside) and the LoginFormValues type. Fields and buttons are the library's input and button items, which install alongside it. `variant` is default | split | glass | minimal | liquid-glass | ribbon-drift. `onSubmit` receives the validated credentials; without it the form simulates a round trip. `signupHref` points at the matching `register-form` page. Validation is client-side presentation only — enforce it again on your server.

items.name: magic-bento
items.title: Magic Bento
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A bento grid whose cards light up and follow the pointer on hover. Use it for feature grids on a landing page.
items.docs: Named exports: MagicBento, MagicBentoCard. Compose cards as children and set `highlight` on the ones that should stand out; span cards across columns with your own grid classes. Layout-agnostic — it supplies the effect, you supply the grid.

items.name: marquee
items.title: Marquee
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A continuously scrolling row or column of content that loops seamlessly. Use it for logo walls and testimonial strips.
items.docs: Duplicate the children set to keep the loop seamless; supports reverse and vertical orientations.

items.name: masonry-grid
items.title: Masonry Grid
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A CSS-column masonry layout with staggered entrance animation. Use it for image galleries and card walls of uneven height.
items.docs: Named export: MasonryGrid. Generic over your item type — pass `items` and a `renderItem` callback. Column count and gaps come from `columnsClassName` and `gapClassName`, so responsive behaviour is plain Tailwind. CSS columns fill top-to-bottom per column, so visual order differs from DOM order.

items.name: masonry-grid-motion
items.title: Masonry Grid (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A CSS-column masonry layout with staggered entrance animation. Use it for image galleries and card walls of uneven height.
items.docs: Motion build of `masonry-grid` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named export: MasonryGrid. Generic over your item type — pass `items` and a `renderItem` callback. Column count and gaps come from `columnsClassName` and `gapClassName`, so responsive behaviour is plain Tailwind. CSS columns fill top-to-bottom per column, so visual order differs from DOM order.

items.name: memories-card
items.title: Memories Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A swipeable stack of photo cards with location, date and tag metadata. Use it for travel, gallery and testimonial carousels.
items.docs: Named export: MemoriesCard. `items` take { id, title, location, date, image, description?, tag? }; `onCardChange` reports the active index. Drag or click to advance the stack.

items.name: memories-card-motion
items.title: Memories Card (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A swipeable stack of photo cards with location, date and tag metadata. Use it for travel, gallery and testimonial carousels.
items.docs: Motion build of `memories-card` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named export: MemoriesCard. `items` take { id, title, location, date, image, description?, tag? }; `onCardChange` reports the active index. Drag or click to advance the stack.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A desktop-style menu bar with click-to-open menus, separators and keyboard navigation. Use it for application chrome rather than website navigation.
items.docs: Named exports: Menubar, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarSeparator. Once a menu is open, hovering another trigger switches to it — the File/Edit/View behaviour of a native app.

items.name: mobile-mockup
items.title: Mobile Mockup
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Device frames for iPhone (5 through 17 Pro Max), Samsung and Pixel that wrap a screenshot, video or live children. Use them to present an app on a marketing page.
items.docs: Named exports: Iphone17ProMaxMockup, Iphone14ProMaxMockup, Iphone12ProMaxMockup, Iphone5Mockup, SamsungS24UltraMockup, GooglePixel8Mockup, GooglePixel10Mockup. Each takes `src`, `videoSrc`, or arbitrary children rendered inside the screen. Pure CSS and SVG — no images to ship.

items.name: modal
items.title: Modal
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A composable overlay handling the portal, backdrop, scroll lock, Escape and backdrop dismissal, with no preset layout of its own. Use it when you hold the open state and want the panel to render your own markup.
items.docs: Named exports: Modal, ModalHeader, ModalBody, ModalFooter, plus the ModalProps and ModalSectionProps types. Modal is controlled — pass `isOpen` and `onClose`; there is no trigger and no `type` or `variant`. Size and skin the panel with `contentClassName` and the backdrop with `overlayClassName`; `hideCloseButton` drops the built-in X and `primaryCloseButton` tints it. Pass `ariaLabel` whenever the heading is not inside ModalHeader. Every slot is optional. The documented form example uses `select`. For a trigger-driven dialog with uncontrolled open state, use `dialog`.

items.name: modern-scroll-stack
items.title: Modern Scroll Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sticky scroll-driven service cards stack where cards slide up from below with horizontal fan offsets and smoothly tilt into resting angles as they lock into place.
items.docs: Named export: ModernScrollStack (also default export), DEFAULT_MODERN_SCROLL_STACK_ITEMS, ModernScrollStackItem, and ModernScrollStackProps.

items.name: navbar
items.title: Navbar
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A responsive marketing navbar with logo, links, mobile menu and GSAP entrance animation. Use it as the top bar of a landing page.
items.docs: Named exports: NavbarBlock, getThemeStyles (from navbar-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Variants: default | floating | centered | minimal | glass | spotlight | ecommerce-mega-nav. Links render through `linkComponent` (a plain `a` by default; pass next/link in Next.js). The mobile menu toggles are the `button` item, which installs alongside. For app chrome with dropdown panels, use `navigation-menu`.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation Menu
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A horizontal navigation bar with dropdown panels and a sliding active indicator. Use it for primary site navigation with grouped links.
items.docs: Named exports: NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuTrigger, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuLink, getThemeStyles (from navigation-menu-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Compose the parts; the root tracks active and hovered state and animates the indicator between triggers. Variants: default | minimal | glass.

items.name: network-graph
items.title: Network Graph
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Concentric rings of avatar nodes around a centre node, with a staggered entrance. Use it for community, integration and social-proof sections.
items.docs: Named export: NetworkGraph. `nodes` take { id, ring, image?, fallback?, label?, size? } — `ring` assigns the orbit. Tune spacing with `ringCount`, `baseRadius` and `ringGap`; `animateIn` staggers the reveal. Positions are computed by ring, not by force simulation.

items.name: newsletter
items.title: Newsletter
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sign-up section in three layouts: readers' faces drifting around a centred form, a panel with a pointer glow and a ticker of who just joined, or the form beside a fanned stack of recent issues. The form becomes a thank-you when your promise resolves.
items.docs: Named export: Newsletter, with parts Heading, Intro, Form, Proof, Ticker and Issues. Composed from the input, button, marquee and tilted-card items, which install alongside it. `variant` is portraits | spotlight | issues, each styled for light and dark mode; `portraits` takes up to four faces; `Form` takes `onSubscribe(email)` (a promise holds the busy state), `action`, `successTitle`/`successText`; `accent` pins the glow and button colour; `reveal` is in-view or immediate.

items.name: newsletter-motion
items.title: Newsletter (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sign-up section in three layouts: readers' faces drifting around a centred form, a panel with a pointer glow and a ticker of who just joined, or the form beside a fanned stack of recent issues. The form becomes a thank-you when your promise resolves.
items.docs: Motion build of `newsletter` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named export: Newsletter, with parts Heading, Intro, Form, Proof, Ticker and Issues. Composed from the input, button, marquee and tilted-card items, which install alongside it. `variant` is portraits | spotlight | issues, each styled for light and dark mode; `portraits` takes up to four faces; `Form` takes `onSubscribe(email)` (a promise holds the busy state), `action`, `successTitle`/`successText`; `accent` pins the glow and button colour; `reveal` is in-view or immediate.

items.name: not-found
items.title: Not Found
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A responsive, full-page 404 Hyperspace website section with ambient radial glow, masked cyber grid backdrop, animated compass indicator, and customizable shortcuts.
items.docs: Named export: NotFoundSection (also default export) and NotFoundSectionProps. Ready for drop-in use in Next.js not-found.tsx or standalone 404 routes.

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A segmented one-time-passcode field with auto-advance, paste handling, and backspace navigation. Use it for email or SMS verification steps.
items.docs: Pasting a full code into any cell distributes the digits across all cells.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A page navigator with previous/next controls and truncated page ranges. Use it for paged tables and result lists.
items.docs: Renders framework-agnostic buttons, not router links, so wire navigation through your own handler.

items.name: particle-canvas
items.title: Particle Canvas
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A high-performance text canvas component with organic repulsion physics and wordmark glow variants featuring cursor tracking and scroll-driven rising animations.
items.docs: Named exports: ParticleCanvas, WordmarkGlowCanvas. Default export: ParticleCanvas. Variants: repel | wordmark-glow. Features 2D particle physics, cursor repulsion, scroll-timeline rising letters, and pointer-following radial glow.

items.name: payment
items.title: Payment
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A card payment form with number, expiry month/year selects and a simulated submit state. Use it as the checkout step in a commerce flow.
items.docs: Named export: PaymentBlock. A self-contained example with hardcoded month and year options and a mocked submit — adapt it rather than configuring through props. Depends on `select` and `ui-base`. No payment provider is wired in; never handle raw card numbers without a PCI-compliant processor such as Stripe Elements.

items.name: piano
items.title: Piano
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive Playable Piano component featuring Web Audio API synthesizers, physical keyboard keybindings (A-S-D-F-G-H-J-K-L-; and W-E-T-Y-U-O-P), master volume slider, and toggleable key indicators.
items.docs: Named export: Piano. Supports `defaultVolume` (0 to 1), `defaultShowKeys` (boolean), and `className`. Synthesizes real acoustic piano notes using native Web Audio API.

items.name: platform-grid
items.title: Platform Grid
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Everything a product offers as one hairline grid: small icon-and-name tiles and a few 2×2 features that show a piece of the product on a tilting card. Reveals as a wave from the centre, then a spotlight follows the pointer. Use it as the 'full platform' section of a product site.
items.docs: Named export: PlatformGrid, with parts Tile, Feature, Mock and Pill. Composed from the tilted-card item, which installs alongside it. Cells pack densely (grid-auto-flow: dense) so features stay square at 8, 6, 4, 3 or 2 columns; `reveal` is in-view or immediate; `fadeEdges` masks the outer columns; `accent` pins the hover/spotlight colour, otherwise it follows --primary. Tiles with `href` are links (`linkComponent` for a router Link).

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A floating panel anchored to a trigger, with collision detection and side/align control. Use it for filter menus and inline detail cards.
items.docs: Named exports: Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent. `side` and `align` set the preferred placement; `avoidCollisions` flips it near a viewport edge, with `collisionPadding` as the margin. Zero runtime dependencies — positioning is hand-rolled, not Floating UI. For hover labels use `tooltip`, for right-click use `context-menu`.

items.name: pricing
items.title: Pricing
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A complete pricing system with plan cards, a comparison table, an interactive plan builder and an interactive service checklist.
items.docs: Named exports: PricingCards, PricingBuilder, PricingTable, PricingSlider, PricingTypographic, PricingPlans. The largest pricing item — variants include cards, builder, table, slider, typographic, and interactive service checklist. The tiered cards popular plan features subtle 3D tilt from tilted-card.

items.name: pricing-plan
items.title: Pricing Plan
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Three pricing layouts in one item — basic cards, a feature table and a usage slider that recalculates price. Use the slider variant for consumption-based products.
items.docs: Named exports: BasicPricingPlan, TablePricingPlan, SliderPricingPlan. The heaviest dependency graph in the registry: pulls `ui-badge`, `ui-button`, `ui-card` and `ui-slider`. Note `ui-card` installs to components/ui/card.tsx and will overwrite an existing shadcn card — review before adding to an established project.

items.name: pricing-section
items.title: Pricing Section
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A compact pricing section with monthly and annual toggle. Use it when pricing is one part of a longer landing page rather than its own page.
items.docs: Named export: PricingSection. Self-contained with hardcoded plans — copy and adapt. Uses next/link, so it needs edits outside Next.js. Installs standalone with no registry dependencies.

items.name: pricing-section-v4
items.title: Pricing Section V4
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A refreshed pricing section with a cleaner card treatment and no animation dependency. Use it as the lighter alternative to the GSAP-based pricing sections.
items.docs: Named export: PricingSectionV4. Self-contained with hardcoded plans — copy and adapt. Uses next/link, so it needs edits outside Next.js. No GSAP, so it is the lightest of the pricing items.

items.name: product-card
items.title: Product Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A reusable, prop-driven E-commerce Product Card supporting color swatches, badges, ratings, quick view, and action buttons.
items.docs: Supports variant=('standard' | 'compact' | 'horizontal'), title, price, colors, badge, rating, onAddToCart, onBuyNow, and onQuickView.

items.name: product-details
items.title: Product Details
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A collection of 4 production-ready, high-converting, fully responsive E-commerce Product Details components featuring split galleries, floating cards, bento hero showcases, and color-synced image previews.
items.docs: Named export: ProductDetails. Accepts `variant` (4 variants: modern-split-gallery, floating-card-glass, bento-editorial-showcase, color-sync-gallery), `title`, `price`, `originalPrice`, `description`, `className`. Adaptable across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports.

items.name: profile-page
items.title: Profile Page
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A person's profile as a glass bento page: an aurora backdrop, frosted panels, and a 24-hour dial that shows their working window live. Use it for team directories, member pages and public profiles.
items.docs: Named exports: ProfilePage, WorkdayDial (GlassPanel is re-exported from the glass-panel item, which installs alongside; useSurface comes from its glass-panel-context.ts). useLocalTime is exported from profile-page-hooks.ts, which installs alongside. `ProfilePage` is the glass backdrop and 12-column grid; place `GlassPanel`s inside with `shape` and column spans. `WorkdayDial` takes `timeZone`, `start`, `end`, `place`, `name`.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A themeable progress bar in three forms — a single bar, a multi-segment track, and a ring — with an optional labelled field wrapper. Use it for determinate operations where percentage complete is known.
items.docs: Named exports: Progress, ProgressField, MultiProgress, ProgressSegment, CircularProgress (getThemeStyles lives in progress-theme.ts, useCountUp in progress-hooks.ts; both install alongside). Use ProgressField when you need a label and value readout; use Progress bare inside your own layout. MultiProgress holds ProgressSegment children that share its `max`, each with its own `color`, for breakdowns across one track. CircularProgress draws the same value as a ring — `circleSize` is the diameter, `barSize` the stroke, and children replace the centred percentage (a function child receives the counting value). Everything fills from zero on mount and tweens later changes via the useCountUp hook; `animate={false}` opts out and `duration` sets the mount run.

items.name: qr-code-generator
items.title: QR Code Generator
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A QR code renderer with size, colour and error-correction options. Use it for sharing links, tickets and pairing codes.
items.docs: Named export: QrCodeGenerator. `value` is the encoded string; `level` is L | M | Q | H — higher survives more damage but packs less data. Keep `bgColor` and `fgColor` high-contrast or scanners will fail. Renders to canvas via qrcode.react.

items.name: qr-code-reader
items.title: QR Code Reader
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A camera-based QR scanner that decodes frames in the browser and reports matches. Use it for check-in and pairing flows.
items.docs: Named export: QrCodeReader. `onRead` fires with the decoded string. Requires camera permission **and a secure context** — it works on HTTPS and localhost, and silently fails on plain HTTP. Decoding runs on the main thread via jsQR, so expect load on low-end devices. Handle permission denial in your own UI.

items.name: radial-orbital-timeline
items.title: Radial Orbital Timeline
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A dynamic orbital visualization component that displays nodes in a circular pattern around a central point. Each node represents a data point with title, status, and energy level.
items.docs: Named export: RadialOrbitalTimeline. `nodes` take { id, title, date, status, energyLevel, description, icon?, connectedNodes? }. Click or hover nodes to reveal inspector popover card. Supports `autoRotate`, `rotationSpeed`, and custom accent colors.

items.name: range-date-picker
items.title: Range Date Picker
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive Range Date Picker featuring single month, dual-month, and rate-priced calendar layouts with customizable theme colors.
items.docs: Named export: RangeDatePicker. Supports variant=('single' | 'dual' | 'priced-single' | 'priced-dual'), getPrice, color, value={from, to}, onChange, disablePast / minDate / maxDate. `showTime` adds Start / End time columns: the card opens as a bare calendar (empty when uncontrolled) and a time rail unfolds beside it on the first pick — under it when narrow — and folds away on Clear; `timeFormat` (12h | 24h) and `minuteStep` tune the columns. Installs time-picker alongside.

items.name: register-form
items.title: Register Form
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sign-up form with paired name fields, password confirmation, a terms checkbox and multiple layout variants including ribbon-drift and liquid-glass. Use it wherever new accounts are created.
items.docs: Default export: RegisterForm. Also exports RegisterBlock, getThemeStyles (from register-form-theme.ts, which installs alongside) and the RegisterFormValues type. Fields and buttons are the library's input and button items, which install alongside it. `variant` is default | split | glass | minimal | scenic | liquid-glass | ribbon-drift. `onSubmit` receives the validated fields; without it the form simulates a round trip. `loginHref` points at the matching `login-form` page, and `minPasswordLength` sets the client-side minimum. Validation is client-side presentation only — enforce it again on your server.

items.name: resizable
items.title: Resizable
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Draggable split panes in horizontal or vertical layout, with min and max size constraints. Use it for editor and preview layouts users can rebalance.
items.docs: Named exports: ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle. Sizes are percentages — `defaultSize`, `minSize` and `maxSize` per panel. Set `withHandle` to render a visible grip. Groups nest, so a horizontal split can contain a vertical one.

items.name: reviews
items.title: Reviews
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A high-converting Review and Testimonial section with a 3D rotating background globe, smooth right-to-left marquee cards, and client rating badges.

items.name: scroll-accordion-showcase
items.title: Scroll Accordion Showcase
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A scroll-linked accordion pairing expanding text steps with a synced image panel. Use it for long-form product explainers.
items.docs: Named export: ScrollAccordionShowcase. `displayMode` is both | text-only | image-only; items carry stepNumber, tags and an image. The open step persists via `localStorageKey`. Needs real page height to advance.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll Area
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A scroll container with styled, optionally auto-hiding scrollbars in either axis. Use it to keep scrollbar appearance consistent across browsers.
items.docs: Named exports: ScrollAreaBlock, getThemeStyles (from scroll-area-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `orientation` is vertical | horizontal | both; `autoHide` fades the bar when idle and `hideTrack` drops the track entirely. Needs a bounded height to scroll — give it an explicit height or a flex parent.

items.name: scroll-split-cards
items.title: Scroll Split Cards
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A cinematic scroll-driven storytelling card component that splits a seamless panoramic image into three panels, expands gaps, flips 180° in 3D into editorial narratives, and glides away.
items.docs: Named export: ScrollSplitCards.

items.name: scroll-stack
items.title: Scroll Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Cards that stack and scale as the page scrolls, revealing each in turn. Use it for step-by-step feature walkthroughs.
items.docs: Named exports: ScrollStack, StackItem. `items` take { id, title, description?, content?, color?, icon? }; `depthScale` and `cardGap` tune the stack. Pass `scroller` when the page scrolls inside a container rather than the window. No runtime dependencies.

items.name: secure-envelope
items.title: Secure Envelope
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive classified security envelope & travel pass sleeve component featuring a secret card that glides out horizontally on hover and elevates gracefully onto the cover on click with 3D flip physics.
items.docs: Named export: SecureEnvelope (also ConfidentialFolder).

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A searchable select with single or multiple selection, option groups and per-option icons. Use it when a native <select> cannot carry enough structure.
items.docs: Named exports: SelectBlock, getThemeStyles (from select-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `options` take { label, value, icon?, group? } — supplying `group` renders grouped headings. `value` accepts a string, or an array when multiple selection is enabled. Several other blocks depend on this one.

items.name: selection-frame
items.title: Selection Frame
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: That box Figma draws around a selected layer — corner handles and a crisp accent stroke — around any text span or block. Use it to spotlight a word, a card or a screenshot region in docs and marketing.
items.docs: Named export: SelectionFrame (also exports the FrameHandles and FrameLine types). Wrap any child; it is measured live with a ResizeObserver. `handles` is square | circle, `line` is solid | dashed | long, `dash` overrides the [dash, gap] pair, `animated` marches dashed/long strokes and pops the handles in, `color` is any CSS colour (Figma blue default), `radius` and `padding` are pixels, and `inline={false}` makes it block-level. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: settings
items.title: Settings
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Pre-built settings panels for notification and security preferences, laid out as toggle rows. Use them as a starting point for an account settings page.
items.docs: Named exports: NotificationsBlock, SecurityBlock. These are self-contained example panels with their own local state and hardcoded labels — copy and adapt rather than configuring through props. Depends on `ui-base` for ComponentCard and ToggleSwitch.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A collapsible application sidebar with grouped items, brand header, footer and a mobile drawer. Use it as the primary shell for a dashboard.
items.docs: Named exports: SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarBrand, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarFooter, useSidebar (from sidebar-context.ts, which installs alongside). Wrap your app in SidebarProvider; read `expanded` and `isMobileOpen` from useSidebar to drive your own toggle. Variants: attached | floating. Collapsed item labels show in the `tooltip` item, which installs alongside.

items.name: signup-form
items.title: Signup Form
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A standalone registration form with inline field validation and animated error states. Use it where sign-up is its own page rather than a tab beside sign-in.
items.docs: Named export: SignupForm. Uses Motion for field-level error transitions. Validation is client-side presentation only — enforce it again on your server.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A loading placeholder with a pulse or shimmer sweep. Use it to hold layout space while content is still being fetched.
items.docs: Shimmer keyframes ship inline in a scoped <style> block — no global CSS or Tailwind config changes required.

items.name: social-links
items.title: Social Links
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A row of brand marks that link out — X, GitHub, LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Discord, Dribbble, email. Use it in footers, profile cards and author bylines.
items.docs: Named export: SocialLinks (plus the SocialLink and SocialNetwork types). `links` is { network, href, label? }[]; `variant` is tile | outline | ghost, `size` is sm | md | lg. Links open in a new tab unless `external` is false; mailto links never do. Brand marks are inline SVG, so no icon package is needed.

items.name: sonner
items.title: Sonner
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A stacked toast notifier driven by a module-level function rather than a React context. Use it when you want to fire notifications from outside the component tree.
items.docs: Named exports: Toaster, toast, toastState. Mount Toaster once, then call `toast()` from anywhere — including non-React code — since state lives in a module singleton. Set `expand` to fan the stack apart on hover. For a context-based API, use `toast`.

items.name: split-flap
items.title: Split-Flap Display
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An authentic, physics-driven Split-Flap Display component simulating retro-mechanical flap cards, 3D perspective flips, and synthesized click sounds with ivory and minimalist variants.
items.docs: Named exports: SplitFlap, SPLIT_FLAP_CHARSET. Default export: SplitFlap. Variants: ivory | minimalist. Features 3D mechanical rotateX animation, Web Audio API sound generator, and responsive size presets.

items.name: split-scroll-stack
items.title: Split Scroll Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A two-column scroll stack with a pinned side panel and cards that advance alongside it. Use it for feature tours that pair narrative with visuals.
items.docs: Named export: SplitScrollStack. `stickySide` pins left or right; `cardDepthScale` and `cardOffset` tune the stack. Driven by GSAP ScrollTrigger, so it needs real page height — it will look inert in a short container. Same family as `split-stepper`.

items.name: split-stepper
items.title: Split Stepper
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A two-column stepper with a sticky side panel and stacked cards that advance as you scroll. Use it for onboarding and feature walkthroughs on a landing page.
items.docs: Named export: SplitStepper. `stickySide` places the pinned column left or right; `cardDepthScale` and `cardOffset` tune the stacked-card depth effect. Needs real page height to scroll through — it will look inert inside a short container.

items.name: squircle-carousel
items.title: Squircle Carousel
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Horizontal flowing carousel where images are masked behind a barrel-distorted grid of rounded cubes with snap physics and smooth inertia.
items.docs: Named export: SquircleCarousel. Interactive drag with grab cursor, momentum physics, barrel fisheye distortion, and squircle grid masking.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A horizontal step indicator with icons and GSAP transitions between steps. Use it to show progress through a known, ordered sequence.
items.docs: Named exports: Stepper, StepperContent. `steps` take { id, title, description?, icon?, content? }. Controlled via `currentStep` and `onStepChange` — the component displays progress but does not own it. For the full state machine, use `wizard`.

items.name: sticky-scroll-stack
items.title: Sticky Scroll Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sticky section whose panels swap content as you scroll, supporting list, image, split and custom layouts. Use it for feature sections with varied content per step.
items.docs: Named export: StickyScrollStack. Each item sets `contentType` (list | image | split | custom) so steps need not share a shape. Uses next/image, so it needs edits outside Next.js.

items.name: sticky-scroll-stack-motion
items.title: Sticky Scroll Stack (Motion)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A sticky section whose panels swap content as you scroll, supporting list, image, split and custom layouts. Use it for feature sections with varied content per step.
items.docs: Motion build of `sticky-scroll-stack` — same props, markup and install path; install one or the other. Named export: StickyScrollStack. Each item sets `contentType` (list | image | split | custom) so steps need not share a shape. Uses next/image, so it needs edits outside Next.js.

items.name: support-container
items.title: Support Container
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A support ticket list with filters, detail view and empty state, configured through one content object. Use it to drop a help-desk view into an existing layout.
items.docs: Named export: SupportContainer. Configured via a single nested prop object covering header, filters, tickets, emptyState and detailView — all copy is passed in, so it localises without edits. Installs standalone with no registry dependencies.

items.name: support-dashboard
items.title: Support Dashboard
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A full help-desk dashboard with tickets, SLA tracking, contact details and chat or table layouts. Use it as the agent-facing side of a support product.
items.docs: Named exports: SupportDashboard, plus Ticket, TicketContact, TicketSLA, TicketMessage and SupportData types. `layout` switches between chat and table views over the same ticket data. Depends on `select`. The most feature-complete block in the registry — expect to replace its demo data wholesale.

items.name: support-hero
items.title: Support Hero
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A product hero on a soft grey ground: a headline that rises in word by word, one line and one call to action, then a bento of frosted cards — integrations, two figures that count up, two portraits and a team card with faces scattered over it. Use it as the opening section of a SaaS or AI product site.
items.docs: Named export: SupportHero, with parts Card, Integrations, Stat, Photo and Team. Composed from the glass-panel, text-animation, counter and button items, which install alongside it. Cards land in one staggered pass after the headline (`reveal` in-view or immediate); Stats count up when on screen; hover lifts cards, zooms portraits and drifts the faces. `cta` takes a label plus `onClick` or `href`.

items.name: support-page
items.title: Support Page
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A customer-facing support page with ticket list, reply composer and details sidebar. Use it as the end-user counterpart to the agent dashboard.
items.docs: Named export: SupportPage. Configured through one nested content object covering header, filters, tickets, replySection and detailsSection. Depends on `select`. For the agent-side view with SLA tracking, use `support-dashboard`.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Composable table primitives — you write the rows, so no column config and no required data shape. Use it for tabular data you want full control over.
items.docs: Named exports: Table, TableHeading, TableContent, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableFooter, TableEmpty, TableExpandedRow, TableExpandToggle, TableRowActions, useTableStyles, getThemeStyles. Each primitive renders its native element and forwards refs, so `colSpan` and aria attributes pass through. Variant (default | minimal | glass | soft), size (sm | md | lg) and color are set once on `Table` and read from context; `soft` is the admin-dashboard look (rounded panel, tinted header band, pill controls, round row actions). Also exports the stateful DataTable family — DataTableTabs, DataTableFilter, DataTableReset, DataTableBatchAction — and the cell/toolbar parts TableAction, TableRowAction, TableBadge and TablePerson. `sticky` on TableHead/TableCell pins a column to the right edge. Sorting and expansion are controlled props — the component never reorders your data. For search, paging, selection and batch actions wired up for you, use `advanced-table`.

items.name: table-of-contents
items.title: Table Of Contents
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive Table of Contents navigation block with sticky right-side positioning, real-time scroll-spy, animated Motion indicators, and section search filtering.
items.docs: Named export: TableOfContentsBlock. Accepts `headings` array of ({ id, title, level }) objects, `showProgress`, `showSearch`, and `color` props. Wraps document content on the left while keeping the TOC sticky on the right.

items.name: tech-stack
items.title: Tech Stack
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The tools a product is built with: a label, then one group of marks at a time in two rows — an odd group as three over four — each mark blurring out and the next group blurring in. Use it as the "Built with" line in a hero or footer.
items.docs: Named exports: TechStack, TechStackGroup and TechStackTool. Compose it: holds children, each holding (icon is any node — an inline SVG or an ). One group shows at a time and gives way to the next every `interval` ms (default 3600; 0 holds the first), only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the swap is a cut. `variant` is labelled (label on the left, names beside marks from xl up) or compact (label centred between hairlines, marks only, names as tooltips and screen-reader text). `label` takes any node. Four to eight tools per group read well. Colours are theme tokens.

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A terminal-styled code block with a title bar, window controls and copy button. Use it to present install and CLI commands the way a reader expects to see them.
items.docs: Named exports: TerminalBlock, getThemeStyles (from terminal-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `code` is the only required prop; `language` defaults to bash and also understands sh, shell, terminal, html, xml, css and a generic JS/TS fallback. `filename` fills the title bar and `copyable` toggles the copy button. Variants: default | glass | minimal. Highlighting is a built-in regex tokenizer, not Shiki or Prism — good for snippets, not a full editor. For several files behind tabs, use `custom-code-block`.

items.name: text-animation
items.title: Text Animation
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Character and word-level text motion driven by Motion. Use it for hero headlines that need finer control than a whole-block fade.
items.docs: Named export: TextAnimation. `text` is a plain string it splits internally; `as` sets the rendered element and `delay` / `duration` control timing; `renderWord(word, index)` swaps what a word renders as on the word-level variants (pop-in, flip, blur-in-up) while keeping its entrance. For dependency-free effects, use `animated-typography`.

items.name: theme-switcher
items.title: Theme Switcher
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A light/dark toggle in icon, pill or dropdown form, with a circular reveal that grows out of the control and a GSAP icon transition. Use it in a navbar or settings panel.
items.docs: Named export: ThemeSwitcher. Variants: icon | pill | dropdown — dropdown includes a system option. Switching runs a circular View-Transition reveal from the clicked control; the CSS it needs is injected by the component, so nothing goes in globals.css. `reveal={false}` for an instant switch. Requires `next-themes` with a ThemeProvider mounted above it; without one it renders but will not change the theme.

items.name: tilted-card
items.title: Tilted Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A card that tilts in 3D toward the pointer with a moving glare highlight. Use it to make a single feature or product card feel tactile.
items.docs: Named export: TiltedCard. Wraps arbitrary children; tune `tiltIntensity`, `glareOpacity` and `scaleOnHover`. Pointer-driven, so it is inert on touch — keep the content readable without the effect.

items.name: time-picker
items.title: Time Picker
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Scrollable hour / minute / AM-PM columns for choosing a time of day, with themed selection and disabled ranges. The building block behind the date pickers' time mode.
items.docs: Named export: TimePicker. The setTime, roundToStep and formatTime helpers live in time-picker-utils.ts, which installs alongside. `value` is a Date whose day is preserved on change; `format` is 12h | 24h, `minuteStep` sets granularity, and `minTime` / `maxTime` disable times outside a window on that day. Used by `date-picker` and `range-date-picker` when `showTime` is on.

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A vertical event timeline with status states, icons and GSAP scroll reveal. Use it for order tracking and process status where each step is done, current or upcoming.
items.docs: Named exports: TimelineBlock, getThemeStyles (from timeline-theme.ts, which installs alongside). Items take { id, title, date, description?, icon?, status } where status is completed | current | upcoming and drives the colour. `layout` places entries left | center | right. For entrance animation variety without status semantics, use `animated-timeline`.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A provider-based toast system with six screen positions, action buttons and auto-dismiss. Use it for transient confirmations triggered from anywhere in the tree.
items.docs: Named exports: ToastProvider (ToastBlock.tsx) and useToast (toast-context.ts, which installs alongside). Wrap your app in ToastProvider, then call `toast()` from useToast. Types: success | error | info | warning | default; `variant` is default | glow | glass | minimal. Set `stack` on the provider to pile toasts behind the newest one (hover fans them out). Set `duration` to 0 to require manual dismissal; hovering pauses the timer. `sonner` does the same job with a module-level API and no provider.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A two-state switch with controlled and uncontrolled modes. Use it for settings that apply immediately, rather than a checkbox in a submitted form.
items.docs: Named export: Toggle. Forwards a ref and accepts `checked` / `onCheckedChange` for controlled use, or `defaultChecked` for uncontrolled.

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: Toggle Group
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A set of toggle buttons behaving as either radio group or checkbox group. Use it for view switches and filter bars where all options should stay visible.
items.docs: Named exports: ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem, getThemeStyles. Set `type` to single or multiple — `value` is a string for single, an array for multiple. Compose ToggleGroupItem children; the group passes theme and size down. `color` accepts primary (the theme token), indigo, rose, emerald, zinc or a hex. `variant="segmented"` is a pill track whose highlight slides to the pressed item; a single segmented group keeps its choice when clicked again and moves it with the arrow keys.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A portal-rendered tooltip with fade and zoom entrance, positioned on hover or focus. Use it for short labels that clarify an unlabeled control.
items.docs: Named exports: TooltipProvider, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent. Requires the `animate-in`, `fade-in` and `zoom-in-95` utilities — on Tailwind v4 add `@import "tw-animate-css";` to your global stylesheet, on v3 use the `tailwindcss-animate` plugin. Content renders through a React portal at z-index 9999.

items.name: top-destinations
items.title: Top Destinations
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A dual-row scroll-driven destination showcase with opposite-direction GSAP ScrollTrigger parallax travel, full-bleed photography, and interactive hover details.
items.docs: Named exports: TopDestinations, TopDestinationsCard, DEFAULT_DESTINATIONS (plus DestinationItem type). Accepts items array or row1Items/row2Items, scrollOffset, and scrollerRef.

items.name: ui-accordion
items.title: UI Accordion
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The Radix-backed accordion primitive that the higher-level Accordion block composes. Install it only if you want the unstyled base directly.
items.docs: Named exports: Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent. This is the internal primitive — most projects want the `accordion` item instead. Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: ui-avatar
items.title: UI Avatar
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The Radix avatar primitive with image and fallback slots. Used for user representation in the chat, support and dashboard blocks.
items.docs: Named exports: Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback. Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: ui-badge
items.title: UI Badge
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A small status label primitive with CVA-driven variants. Used internally by pricing blocks.
items.docs: Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: ui-base
items.title: UI Base
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Shared layout scaffolding (ComponentCard, ToggleSwitch) used by the settings, payment, compute and utility blocks.
items.docs: Named exports: ComponentCard, ToggleSwitch. Pulled in automatically as a dependency — rarely installed directly.

items.name: ui-button
items.title: UI Button
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A minimal CVA button primitive with Radix Slot support for `asChild`. Used internally by the Calendar and pricing blocks.
items.docs: This is the internal primitive, not the main `button` item. Prefer `button` unless you specifically need the Slot-based base. Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: ui-card
items.title: UI Card
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The card surface primitive that the pricing-plan block composes.
items.docs: NOTE: installs to components/ui/card.tsx and will overwrite a shadcn `card` already present. Review before installing into an existing project.

items.name: ui-code-renderer
items.title: UI Code Renderer
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Shiki-backed syntax highlighting for a single snippet, with matched light and dark themes, a shared cached highlighter and a non-shifting fallback while a cold snippet resolves.
items.docs: Named export: CodeRenderer, plus `warmHighlighter` and `prefetchHighlight` for callers that know a snippet before it is shown — prefetching one makes its first paint already highlighted, with no unstyled flash. Takes `code` and a Shiki `lang`. One Shiki instance and one markup cache are shared by every block on the page. A snippet that is still cold renders inside `pre.shiki-pending`; style that class to match your `.shiki` metrics so the swap does not shift the page. Pulled in automatically by `ui-codeblocks` — install it directly only if you are building your own code surface.

items.name: ui-codeblocks
items.title: UI Codeblocks
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A compact code surface with syntax colouring and a copy button, used inside the docs site. Install it for a lightweight code display without tabs.
items.docs: Named export: CodeBlocks. The minimal internal code viewer — for multi-file tabs and filename headers, use `custom-code-block`; for CLI commands, use `terminal`. Installs `ui-code-renderer` alongside it, which brings in Shiki.

items.name: ui-fluid-glass-slider
items.title: UI Fluid Glass Slider
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A glass-morphism slide viewer with fluid GSAP transitions between panels. Use it for hero galleries with a soft, liquid feel.
items.docs: Named export: FluidGlassSlider. Slides take { id, image, title, subtitle }. Installs standalone with no registry dependencies — not even `utils`.

items.name: ui-liquid-glass
items.title: UI Liquid Glass
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: TODO: describe ui-liquid-glass. Generated placeholder.

items.name: ui-multi-select
items.title: UI Multi Select
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A multi-select combobox with search, clearable chips, hierarchical options and optional portal rendering. Use it when users pick several values from a long list.
items.docs: Named export: MultiSelect. Set `hierarchical` with nested `children` options for parent/child groups, and `portal` to escape a clipping overflow container. `isMulti` and `isClearable` are independent, so it also works as a searchable single select.

items.name: ui-sheet
items.title: UI Sheet
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The Radix dialog-based sheet primitive that slides in from a screen edge. Used for drawers and mobile navigation panels.
items.docs: Named exports: Sheet, SheetTrigger, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetFooter, SheetTitle, SheetDescription. Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: ui-slider
items.title: UI Slider
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: The Radix slider primitive used by pricing blocks for usage-based tier selection.
items.docs: Derived from shadcn/ui (MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn).

items.name: upload
items.title: Upload
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A drag-and-drop file dropzone with per-file progress, previews, retry and time-remaining. Use it for multi-file uploads where users need to watch each file land.
items.docs: Named exports: Dropzone, UploadItem, formatBytes, formatTimeLeft. Dropzone handles the drop target and reports via `onFilesDrop`; render an UploadItem per file and drive its `status` and `progress` yourself. No transport is included — wire it to your own upload call.

items.name: user-graph
items.title: User Graph
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An orbital diagram placing a user at the centre with tools and sub-agents circling around. Use it to illustrate an AI agent or integration ecosystem.
items.docs: Named exports: UserGraph. Takes orbiting tools, sub-apps and sub-agents, each with its own icon and colour tokens. Presentational — the layout is decorative, not a real graph engine, so it will not lay out arbitrary node counts gracefully.

items.name: utility
items.title: Utility
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Two small dashboard panels — a team member list and a command search box — built on the shared card shell. Use them as filler panels while assembling a dashboard layout.
items.docs: Named exports: TeamMembersBlock, CommandSearchBlock. Self-contained examples with hardcoded content — copy and adapt rather than configuring through props. Depends on `ui-base`.

items.name: verify-badge
items.title: Verify Badge
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A small verified checkmark badge with an optional draw-in animation. Use it beside names and handles to mark a confirmed account.
items.docs: Named export: VerifyBadge. Sizes are sm | md | lg | xl, `color` takes any CSS colour, and `animate` plays the check-draw on mount.

items.name: vertical-tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A tab panel whose rail runs across the top or down the side, with GSAP transitions between panels. Use it for settings and documentation sections with long content.
items.docs: Named exports: VerticalTabs, getThemeStyles (from vertical-tabs-theme.ts, which installs alongside). `tabs` take { id, label, icon?, content }. `orientation` defaults to horizontal and switches to vertical without changing the API. Variants: default | glass | minimal | bordered | underline | segmented | soft | elevated — every one renders in both orientations. Ships full tablist semantics: arrow keys along the rail, Home/End, and a focus ring drawn in your accent. `underline` and `segmented` move a single measured indicator between tabs; motion is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: video-accordion
items.title: Video Accordion
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: Horizontal panels that expand on selection to play a video, with poster fallbacks. Use it for product feature showcases.
items.docs: Named exports: VideoAccordion, AccordionPanel. Panels take { id, title, description?, videoSrc, posterUrl? }; `defaultActiveId` sets the initially open one. Videos load per panel — keep them short and muted, since autoplay with sound is blocked by browsers.

items.name: video-player
items.title: Video Player
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A video hero with thumbnail and glow that plays in a modal, inline in the card, or directly on load — behind a YouTube embed or a native HTML5 video.
items.docs: Named export: VideoPlayer. `videoUrl` and `thumbnailUrl` drive it; `playbackMode` is modal | inline | direct and `source` is youtube | video (a native <video>). `aspectRatio` is 16/9 | 21/9 | 4/3 | 1/1 and `modalSize` is md | lg | xl | full. `onPlay` and `onClose` hook into analytics. In modal and inline the media only loads on click, so it stays off the initial page weight; `direct` renders it immediately and honours `autoPlay` / `muted` / `loop`.

items.name: video-player-jw
items.title: Video Player (JW Player)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A hero video player built on JW Player, with colour skin presets and a native fallback for when the licensed library is unavailable.
items.docs: Named exports: JwPlayer, JW_DEMO_LIBRARY_URL, plus the JwSkinConfig and JwSkinPreset types. No npm dependency — the JW library is a licensed remote script loaded from `libraryUrl`. It defaults to JW's public documentation library, which is fine to evaluate against but must be replaced with your own `https://cdn.jwplayer.com/libraries/<PLAYER_ID>.js` before shipping; a self-hosted build also needs `licenseKey`. `skin` picks a colour preset (default | midnight | neon | sunset | minimal), `skinConfig` takes a raw JW skin object, and `skinUrl` / `skinName` point at a custom stylesheet. If the library fails to load the component falls back to a native <video> rather than a black box.

items.name: video-player-plyr
items.title: Video Player (Plyr)
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A hero video player built on Plyr — one accessible, skinnable control bar in front of HTML5 files, YouTube and Vimeo alike.
items.docs: Named export: PlyrPlayer. Requires the `plyr` package, which the CLI installs. `provider` is html5 | youtube | vimeo and `mediaType` is video | audio; `accentColor` sets Plyr's `--plyr-color-main`, and `controls` takes Plyr's control-name array. Plyr is imported dynamically inside an effect, so the component server-renders cleanly. Its control icons come from Plyr's CDN sprite by default — set `iconUrl` to a self-hosted `plyr.svg` if the page must not reach a third-party host.

items.name: waitlist
items.title: Waitlist
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A pre-launch sign-up in three layouts: a compact card, a brand mark with a live countdown over the form, or a pill on a soft ground with the faces already in and a bar of the spots claimed. The form becomes the reader's place in line — a number that counts up, and an invite link to copy — when your promise resolves.
items.docs: Named export: Waitlist, with parts Mark, Countdown, Heading, Intro, Form, Proof and Spots. Composed from the counter, input, button, avatar-stack, progress and copy-button items, which install alongside it. `variant` is card | launch | queue, each styled for light and dark mode; `Countdown` takes a `date` and is the counter's slide countdown; `Form` takes `onJoin(email)` — resolve a number to show it as the place in line, throw an Error to show its message — plus `action`, `shareUrl`, `note` and the success copy; `Spots` takes `claimed` and `total`; `accent` pins the colour; `reveal` is in-view or immediate.

items.name: wallet
items.title: Wallet
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: An interactive fintech cardholder wallet component featuring 3 serially staggered cards, curved pocket scoop, bottom thumb cutout, and light/dark mode styling.
items.docs: Named export: Wallet. Accepts cards array, overallBalance, allowReveal, and autoRevealOnHover.

items.name: wizard
items.title: Wizard
items.author: AlgorizeTech
items.description: A multi-step form flow with context-driven navigation, progress bar and completion callback. Reach for it when a form is long enough to need splitting across steps.
items.docs: Named exports: Wizard, WizardProgress, WizardContainer, WizardStep, WizardTitle, WizardDescription, useWizard. Wizard owns the step state; children read `currentStep`, `nextStep` and `prevStep` from the useWizard hook. `onComplete` fires on the final step. Unlike `stepper`, this manages navigation for you.
